sections.h2: Where do I record a deed in Graves County, KY?
sections.html:
Take it to the Graves County Clerk in Mayfield. Under KRS 382.110, an instrument has to be recorded where the land lies, or where most of the land lies if it straddles a county line. Filing anywhere else leaves the deed exposed to later buyers who had no notice of it and to creditors.

The Clerk works from 1102 Paris Road, Suite 5, Mayfield, KY 42066, and the county lists its hours as eight to four-thirty. The county's own page describes the office as the keeper of deeds, mortgages and encumbrances. Real estate records are handled through the records vault, (270) 247-1697, while title transfers, marriage licenses and vehicle work go through (270) 247-1676.

Delinquent real estate tax is collected at the same office, so an owner with an old balance can pay it and file the deed during one trip.

sections.h2: What are the Graves County Clerk's recording fees?
sections.html:
KRS 64.012 sets the schedule, and the version in force since July 15, 2026 charges $33 to record and index a deed of up to five pages. A mortgage of up to 30 pages is $63. Each page past the limit adds $3, and the Clerk can also collect a $10 reimbursement for permanent storage of the record.

Selected Clerk fees under KRS 64.012 (source: Kentucky Revised Statutes, current through the 2026 session)
ServiceFee
Deed, indexed and recorded, five pages or fewer$33.00
Extra page on a deed$3.00
Extra cross-reference to the same instrument$4.00
Mortgage, 30 pages or fewer$63.00
Deed of release for a mortgage or lien$33.00
Notary acknowledgment on a deed$5.00
Certified copy$5.00, then $0.50 per page beyond three
Plat or survey up to 24 by 36 inches$40.00 per page

The statute splits each $33 deed fee: $27 stays with the Clerk and $6 goes to the state affordable housing trust fund. A seller who needs the Clerk to notarize the deed should budget the $5 on top.

sections.h2: What must a Kentucky deed say before the Clerk will accept it?
sections.html:
KRS 382.135 forbids the Clerk from filing a deed that leaves out required items, so mistakes are stopped at the counter. The deed has to contain:

  • the grantor's and grantee's complete names, and a mailing address for each;
  • the full price or other consideration;
  • an in-care-of address for the property tax bill of the year of transfer;
  • a notarized certificate from both parties confirming that the stated price is the whole consideration, or, for a gift, saying so and giving an estimate of fair cash value.

KRS 382.110 adds a lineage requirement. The deed must point to the grantor's own source of title, giving the office, book, page and recording date of the earlier deed. If the owner inherited the land, the deed says how and from whom.

Utility easement deeds, cemetery lot deeds, government rights-of-way and deeds that fix errors in an earlier deed are exempt from the price, tax-address and certificate items.

sections.h2: How does an inherited Graves County house reach the buyer?
sections.html:
If the owner died and the house passed under a will or by intestate succession, the estate's personal representative must file an affidavit in each county where the estate owns property, before the estate is closed out. It names the people receiving each parcel and the value assigned in handling the estate, or says no value was set.

A Graves County heir selling to a cash buyer should therefore expect two filings at the Clerk's office, the affidavit and the new deed, with the deed charged under the schedule above.

KRS 382.270 adds one more gate. A deed or mortgage does not protect against a buyer for value without notice, or against creditors, until it has been acknowledged or proved as the law directs.

sections.h2: Who pays the transfer tax on a Graves County sale?
sections.html:
The seller pays it, under KRS 142.050, and the Clerk collects it when the deed is offered for recording. The rate is $0.50 for each $500 of value, rounded up. At the Census median value of $147,800 that comes to 296 units, or $148.

Several kinds of transfer are excused, including transfers to secure or release a debt, between spouses in a divorce, and in foreclosure. The Grayson County Clerk page on this site lists the exemptions in more detail.

sections.h2: How are mortgage releases and assignments handled?
sections.html:
A paid-off mortgage is cleared with a release recorded at the Clerk's office. KRS 382.360 permits a margin entry or a separate deed of release, and it spells out that giving the release to the borrower does not satisfy the duty to file it. A seller whose lender never filed can discover the old mortgage still open on the record.

When a lender passes a mortgage to another holder, the new holder files the assignment within 30 days. Missing that deadline does not by itself affect the lien's validity.

A mortgage that keeps a lien in the deed also has to name the source of the borrower's title, and KRS 382.290 lets the Clerk charge the KRS 64.012 fee for each assignment and release noted on the record, paid by the person making the entry.

Ask the records vault before listing whether each earlier mortgage on the parcel shows as released. An open mortgage that was actually paid is easier to fix before a buyer's title search finds it.

sections.h2: How do I get a certified copy of a recorded Graves County deed?
sections.html:
Ask the records vault. A certified copy of any record is $5, plus $0.50 for each page beyond the third, under KRS 64.012. KRS 382.110 treats an authentic photocopy that the official custodian certifies as a true, unaltered copy of the original, and a certified copy can be filed in another county's office as if it were the original, provided it meets all the filing rules.

That matters when a parcel crosses a county line or when a lender wants proof of an earlier deed. Owners selling inherited land often need a certified copy of the last vesting deed to give the title company.

  • Bring the grantor name, the approximate year and, if you have them, the deed book and page.
  • Ask whether the copy needs to carry the clerk's certification for out-of-county use.
  • Request a separate copy of any recorded release, so the chain from deed to payoff is complete.

sections.h2: What is Graves County like for a seller?
sections.html:
Graves County sits in far western Kentucky and was formed in 1824. Mayfield is the seat. The county also holds Wingo, a stretch of the Clarks River National Wildlife Refuge, and the Black Patch tobacco history that shaped its farms. A December 10, 2021 tornado caused major damage in Mayfield, including to the courthouse. Census QuickFacts reports:

  • 37,050 residents in 2025 and 14,139 households.
  • A 76.1 percent owner-occupied rate and a median value of $147,800.
  • Median gross rent of $775.
  • Retail sales of $808,990,000 in 2022, or $22,168 per person.

A seller who keeps the recorded paperwork in order, from the last vesting deed to the mortgage release, avoids the delays that title problems cause.

faqs.q: Which office files deeds for a house in Graves County?
faqs.a: The Graves County Clerk, 1102 Paris Road, Suite 5, Mayfield. Call the records vault at (270) 247-1697 with questions about real estate filings.

faqs.q: What does recording a deed cost in Graves County?
faqs.a: $33 for up to five pages under KRS 64.012, plus $3 for each extra page and a $10 storage reimbursement. The seller's transfer tax is separate.

faqs.q: Can the Clerk turn my deed away?
faqs.a: Yes. KRS 382.135 bars filing a deed that lacks names, addresses, the consideration statement, a tax-bill address or the sworn certificate, and the deed must also cite its source of title.

faqs.q: Is a mortgage release my lender's job or mine?
faqs.a: The lender or holder signs it, but it only counts once it is filed with the Clerk. Handing a copy to the borrower is not enough, so ask the records vault whether it appears on your parcel.

faqs.q: What do heirs file before selling an inherited Graves County house?
faqs.a: The estate's personal representative files an affidavit with the Clerk listing each recipient and the estimated value, and the new deed follows. KRS 382.135 requires the affidavit before the estate closes.
